pr.title: feat(tour): plan agent tours with your own agent command
pr.body: Adds the first agent tour style. `--style agentTour` (or `stk.tourStyle = agentTour`) has an agent plan each review: an overview, the files in reading order as titled steps with a short explanation each, and notes on particular lines. - The agent is your own command: `stk.tourAgent` or `--agent`, such as `claude -p` or `llm -m `. It holds its own credentials, so git-stk holds none. `src/agent.rs` is the one place it runs: split into words like a simple shell command line (no shell), the request on stdin, the answer from stdout, a 10-minute timeout, and its stderr on failure. - The request is the review's description, commits, stack position, and diff (cut short per file and overall; generated files by name only), with the plan format. The answer may wrap the JSON plan in prose, a fence, or a CLI's own `result` envelope. - The plan is checked against the diff: unknown paths dropped, each file once, files left out gathered into an "Other changes" step, notes only on lines the diff shows. A plan that places nothing, or an agent that fails, leaves that review toured by file role, with a warning. - The first agent tour in a repository asks before sending anything and records `stk.tourAgentAllowed` in that repository's config; without a terminal it stops and says how to allow it. - Plans are saved per review head and agent command under `.git/stk/tours/plans/`; `--refresh-plan` asks again. `--plan ` follows a plan written ahead of time for the review asked for. - Each chapter's page data carries the plan: the command that planned it and the provider, model, and effort level the agent reports for itself, the overview, and the notes. The next PR shows them on the page; here the plan drives the step order, titles, and explanations. Verified with `just test` (word splitting, the runner, plan parsing from prose/fences/envelopes, validation and corrections, the request; integration tests with a fake agent for a planned tour and its cache and `--refresh-plan`, config vs. `--style`, refusing without consent, `--plan`, and an unusable answer or failing agent falling back), `just lint`, and live with `claude -p` on #371 (35 s) and #364 (57 s, 11 files in seven well-ordered steps, ten notes kept, no corrections). -
